title: Stanford CS229 main notes, Spring 2026 (Ma and Ng)
why: Primary source for the derivations: normal equations, logistic loss, GLMs, GDA, naive Bayes, SVM dual, bias variance, double descent, EM and PCA.

title: Stanford CS229 Spring 2026 course page
why: Teaching team and course structure for the Spring 2026 lectures linked in this module.

title: Chip Huyen, ML Interviews Book: classic ML questions
why: Real interview questions on kNN, k-means versus GMM, bagging versus boosting, naive Bayes and SVMs.

title: Chip Huyen, ML Interviews Book: ML basics
why: Questions on learning settings, empirical risk, parametric models and why L1 gives sparsity.

title: Chip Huyen, ML Interviews Book: sampling and creating training data
why: Questions on class imbalance, missing data, oversampling leakage and split design.

title: Chip Huyen, ML Interviews Book: objectives, metrics and evaluation
why: Questions on bias variance, cross validation, F1, log loss versus MSE and RMSE versus MAE.

title: Alexey Grigorev, data science interview theory questions
why: A broad bank of screening questions on regression, validation, regularisation, trees, boosting, clustering and time series.

title: scikit-learn: common pitfalls and recommended practices
why: Canonical leakage examples, including feature selection before the split, and the fix with pipelines.

title: scikit-learn: cross validation
why: Every splitter (stratified, grouped, time series) with its guarantees, plus the cross_val_predict warning.

title: scikit-learn: probability calibration
why: Reliability diagrams, typical miscalibration by model family, Platt versus isotonic, and proper scoring rules.

title: scikit-learn: permutation feature importance
why: Why permutation importance on held out data beats impurity importance, and the correlated features caveat.

title: scikit-learn: clustering
why: k-means assumptions, DBSCAN point types, HDBSCAN, linkage behaviour and clustering metrics.

title: Breiman (2001), Random Forests
why: The strength and correlation bound and the out of bag error estimate.

title: Chen and Guestrin (2016), XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System
why: Regularised objective, second order leaf weights and split gain, sparsity aware splits.

title: Ke et al. (2017), LightGBM: A Highly Efficient Gradient Boosting Decision Tree
why: GOSS and exclusive feature bundling, and the reported speedup over conventional GBDT.

title: Prokhorenkova et al., CatBoost: unbiased boosting with categorical features
why: Target leakage in target statistics, prediction shift, ordered target statistics and ordered boosting.

title: Arthur and Vassilvitskii (2007), k-means++: The Advantages of Careful Seeding
why: The D squared seeding rule and its log k competitive guarantee.

title: Saito and Rehmsmeier (2015), The precision recall plot is more informative than the ROC plot on imbalanced datasets
why: Why ROC hides poor precision under imbalance, with worked numbers and PR interpolation pitfalls.

title: Lin et al. (2017), Focal Loss for Dense Object Detection
why: Definition of focal loss and the gamma and alpha settings that worked best.

title: Lundberg and Lee (2017), A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions
why: SHAP values, their three properties and the uniqueness result.

title: Kapoor and Narayanan (2023), Leakage and the Reproducibility Crisis in ML based Science
why: Taxonomy of leakage, the 41 papers across 30 fields, and the civil war prediction case study.

title: Wattenberg, Viégas and Johnson (2016), How to Use t-SNE Effectively
why: Interactive demonstration of perplexity effects and why t-SNE cluster sizes and distances mislead.

title: UMAP documentation: basic parameters
why: What n_neighbors, min_dist, n_components and metric do, with defaults.

title: statsmodels: stationarity and detrending with ADF and KPSS
why: Opposite null hypotheses of ADF and KPSS and how to combine their verdicts.

title: Robert Nau, Duke: introduction to ARIMA models
why: ARIMA notation, differencing and the special cases such as random walk and simple exponential smoothing.
